taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Ruellia ciliatiflora and places the familiar Texas name Ruellia nudiflora in synonymy. Texas field literature still widely uses R. nudiflora; learner preserves that name as a primary alias.
look_here_first: Start with where the flowers are. Common wild petunia sends a conspicuous peduncled, branching terminal flower stalk above the leaves; the flowers are not sitting directly in the leaf axils. Then confirm mostly glabrous/glabrescent oval-ovate leaves with wavy to low-dentate margins.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center Purola Preserve documents Ruellia nudiflora in the natural flora. Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Acanthaceae specimen index includes three Ruellia nudiflora var. nudiflora specimens. Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed local treatment of Ruellia nudiflora var. nudiflora.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County records under R. nudiflora are accepted for the current R. ciliatiflora concept because Kew explicitly synonymizes that name; preserve the alias rather than duplicating the taxon.

best_field_traits: perennial herb/subshrub with woody or persistent base
stems usually erect to ascending and relatively sparsely branched
opposite oval to ovate leaves, usually rounded to subacute at tip
foliage essentially glabrous to only inconspicuously short-hairy
leaf margins commonly wavy, subentire or low-dentate
inflorescences terminal and upper-axillary, distinctly pedunculate and branching into cymes
purple to violet funnel-shaped flowers elevated above foliage
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Ruellia drummondiana: R. drummondiana bears flowers/cymes directly from leaf axils with essentially no peduncle and has short fine pubescence; its capsules contain only 2–4 seeds. Ruellia humilis: R. humilis also has axillary nearly sessile flowers but is conspicuously long-pilose, especially on stems and leaf margins. Ruellia metziae: R. metziae also has terminal pedunculate flowers but is typically white to pale purple and has somewhat narrower leaves; preserve as a later local comparison.

comparisons.key_distinctions: R. drummondiana bears flowers/cymes directly from leaf axils with essentially no peduncle and has short fine pubescence; its capsules contain only 2–4 seeds. R. humilis also has axillary nearly sessile flowers but is conspicuously long-pilose, especially on stems and leaf margins. R. metziae also has terminal pedunculate flowers but is typically white to pale purple and has somewhat narrower leaves; preserve as a later local comparison.
